title: Of Course The New York Post Blames Minneapolis Shooting On Weed

content_html_sanitized:
Let me begin by saying that there is - or is supposed to be - a difference between journalism (reporting facts) and the editorial pages opinions. (Sometimes it was even called the “Chinese Wall”, but in the real world it was more like a picket fence.)

See Transcript of 1996 Conversation Between the Czar and the Former Managing Editor of New York Times About Medical Marijuana Initiatives Gives Great Insight Into How Marijuana Prohibition Really Works.

 

It was a myth in the glory days of the Times, and today it is a joke at the grotesque NYP:

Robin Westman’s pot connection is another reason to go slow on looser rules for weed By Post Editorial Board Published Aug. 29, 2025

 

It begins, “News that Minneapolis monster Robin Westman worked at a pot shop until just two weeks ago should give pause to those in the White House reportedly pushing President Donald Trump to take a landmark step toward federal approval of marijuana use.”

 

But of course, that is not what the proposed change does. It would simply recognize that marijuana has medical use. The Post editorial board is lying.

See A Very Simple Example of the Incompetence of Reporting on Marijuana Prohibition with link to a similar Post editorial.

And

As Prohibitionists Lie About Rescheduling Cannabis to Recognize Potential Medical Use, American Cancer Society Website Lists “Possible Benefits of Cannabis for People With Cancer”

 

“Nearly 47,000 people died of gun-related injuries in the United States in 2023.”

Does that prove that guns should be illegal? Off topic, but I don’t think so.

 

“Each year in the US, there are 7,756 homicides attributable to (assumed to be caused by) alcohol, and 1,269 of these occur in persons younger than 21 years old.”

Does that prove that alcohol should be illegal? Off topic, but I don’t think so.

 

Will the New York Post report any of this and draw conclusions similar to those on cannabis? Don’t hold your breath, unless you take a big hit first.

 

There were well over 200,000 arrests for marijuana-related violations in 2023, and 84 percent (200,306) were charged with possession only. In all, some 25 percent of all “specified” drug-related arrests reported to the FBI in 2023 were for cannabis-related violations.

 

“Marijuana arrests peaked in the United States in 2007, when police made over 870,000 marijuana-related arrests. At that time, just under half (48 percent) of all drug-related arrests in the United States were for marijuana-related violations.”

There have been more than 30,000,000 marijuana arrests in the last 50 years. Did that stop Americans from using marijuana?

Ninety percent of the American people are in favor of medical cannabis.

Will the Post report any of that? Apparently not. New York deserves better. America deserves better.

Happy Labor Day!
